title: Markets Bet Big on a Quick End to the Iran War
partialText: Global markets rallied as President Trump signaled that the United States may stop fighting soon. But big questions remain about lingering damage.

title: Robot Taxis Stop in Traffic in Chinese City, Stranding Travelers
partialText: The authorities in Wuhan, the site of one of the world’s largest experiments in self-driving cars, cited a “system failure” after widespread reports on Tuesday evening.

title: Markets Extend Rally and Oil Prices Drop After Trump Says Iran War Will Wind Down
partialText: President Trump said the U.S. military would wrap up its campaign in Iran in two or three weeks.

title: Judge Blocks Trump’s Order to End Funding for NPR and PBS
partialText: The ruling will have minimal effect on the federal money going to public media because Congress voted to claw back funding. But it could have implications for any future funding.

title: Allbirds, Once Silicon Valley’s Favorite Shoe, Sells for $39 Million
partialText: Despite once being valued at $4 billion, the company that made sneakers from Merino wool struggled to capture a wide customer base and turn a profit.

title: March Madness Puts Las Vegas Back in the Game
partialText: The influx of fans during this month’s college basketball tournament is a welcome lift to the city’s casinos and hotels after a dismal 2025, when the number of visitors fell 7.5 percent.

title: Global Ban on Digital Duties Expires After Stalled Talks at W.T.O.
partialText: A prohibition on taxing digital downloads expired, after members of the World Trade Organization concluded their annual meeting without an agreement.

title: Eli Lilly Will Buy a Narcolepsy Drug Developer for $6.3 Billion
partialText: Eli Lilly plans to acquire Centessa Pharmaceuticals, which has been conducting a midstage clinical trial of its lead drug.

title: McCormick to Combine With Unilever Food Unit to Create a Spice Giant
partialText: The deal ends Unilever’s time in the food industry and will create a multibillion-dollar group under the McCormick name.

title: FDA Is Expected to Lift Restriction on Peptides, Heeding RFK Jr.’s Wishes
partialText: The peptides, which are increasingly marketed as providing longevity and health benefits, were removed in 2023 from the agency’s list of products that compounding pharmacies can sell.

title: The Trump Effect at the Pump as Gas Hits $4 a Gallon
partialText: The average price of gasoline in the U.S. has topped $4 a gallon, a multiyear high, as war in the Middle East roils the oil market and slams drivers.

title: Stocks Recover Sharply Amid Hope for Iran War’s End
partialText: Investors weighed the news that the owner of a Kuwaiti tanker loaded with oil said it had been hit in an Iranian attack near Dubai.

title: Whoop, a Wearable Health Device Maker, Raises $575 Million
partialText: With elite athletes like LeBron James and Cristiano Ronaldo as investors, the company, now valued at $10 billion, is courting everyday health enthusiasts.

title: As Iran War Pushes Up Gas Prices, Fresh Food Distributors Add Fuel Surcharges
partialText: Delivering salmon, fruits and other perishable foods has become more expensive as the war with Iran pushes up diesel prices.

title: U.S. Gas Prices Hit $4 a Gallon on Average, a ‘Headache’ for Drivers and Trump
partialText: A month since the first U.S.-Israeli attacks and Iran’s response effectively shut off Persian Gulf oil, drivers are paying significantly more to fill up.

title: Employee Lawsuit Against Fox News Is Dismissed
partialText: A reporter who claimed the network had fired him for challenging its coverage failed to prove retaliation and discrimination, a federal judge said.

title: T.S.A. Lines Appear to Be Getting Shorter as Workers Begin to Receive Paychecks
partialText: The hourslong waits appeared to be easing as Transportation Security Administration officers received their first pay in weeks. But with no funding deal, the lines could return.

title: Democrats Examine Elon Musk’s Role in Suspension of Business Disclosure Law
partialText: Lawmakers have asked the Treasury Department for information on how Mr. Musk may have influenced the decision to end enforcement of the Corporate Transparency Act.

title: From Foe to Ally: The S.E.C. Is Now Writing Crypto-Friendly Policies
partialText: The embrace of crypto by financial regulators under President Trump has entered a new, cozier phase.

title: Michael Rousseau, Air Canada’s CEO, to Step Down Amid Backlash Over Comments After Crash
partialText: Michael Rousseau’s mostly English statement after a fatal runway collision drew sharp criticism. The airline said it would emphasize French fluency in its search for a successor.

title: Iran War’s Latest Economic Toll: Oil at $115 a Barrel
partialText: Economists and investors are increasingly pricing in a slowdown, or even a global recession, if the fighting drags on.

title: Private-Credit Wobbles Could Prove Perilous for Trump
partialText: The Trump administration is poised to broaden access to risky investments that are showing signs of strain.

title: How Bard College Became a Major Real Estate Player 20 Miles Away
partialText: A nonprofit foundation donated $82 million worth of properties in Hudson, N.Y., to the school, which has provided few details about its plans.

title: Asia Depends on L.N.G. From the Middle East. This Is What Happens When It Runs Out.
partialText: With a cutoff in shipments imminent, Asian countries, the biggest importers of liquefied natural gas from the Middle East, are already burning more coal and reducing consumption.

title: Oil Wavers on Mixed Signals in Middle East Talks
partialText: Investors digested increasing signs of escalation of the U.S.-Israeli war in Iran, which has led to a blockage of critical energy supplies.

title: Politico Names Jonathan Greenberger as New Editor
partialText: Jonathan Greenberger, an executive at the publication, will take over from John Harris, a co-founder of Politico.

title: New Political Group to Push Trump’s A.I. Agenda in Midterms
partialText: The group, Innovation Council Action, says it plans to spend at least $100 million. It will be led by a former administration official.

title: ICE May Remain at Airports Even After T.S.A. Pay Resumes, Border Czar Says
partialText: Transportation safety officers are set to be paid on Monday, but Tom Homan, the White House’s border czar, said ICE agents may stay where there are shortages.

title: How Many Air Traffic Controllers Are Needed Overnight?
partialText: The accident at LaGuardia has raised questions about whether the minimum standard of two air traffic controllers on overnight shifts is sufficient.

title: Why the Iran War May Force Countries to Rely Less on Natural Gas
partialText: The U.S. and other exporters are poised for a windfall, but disruptions to Persian Gulf supplies are also pushing gas-buying countries to consider alternatives like coal, solar and nuclear energy.

title: He Was Supposed to Break Up Kraft and Heinz. He Changed His Mind.
partialText: Steve Cahillane, a food industry veteran, is trying to revive the company behind Kool-Aid, Oscar Mayer and many other brands.

title: The Fragile Hope for Salmon Recovery in Maine
partialText: A long-term project to remove or modify dams may clear the way for endangered wild Atlantic salmon to swim freely up to the Sandy River. But it faces opposition from business and lawmakers.

title: Chromebook Remorse: Tech Backlash at Schools Extends Beyond Phones
partialText: No more YouTube or video games on school laptops. Textbooks and pencils are back. Some seventh graders say they prefer learning offline.

title: Check Your Target-Date Fund, Especially if You Plan to Retire Soon
partialText: Their simplicity makes the funds appealing, but they could leave many workers near retirement, particularly baby boomers, short on savings.

title: The Air Canada Crash: Before and After the Frantic Call to ‘Stop, Stop, Stop’
partialText: How a cascade of seemingly minor events led to the worst runway disaster at LaGuardia Airport in decades.

title: 10 Million Grill Brushes Recalled After Some People Ingested Loose Bristles
partialText: In at least five cases, customers sought medical attention to remove bristles “from their digestive tract or throat,” a federal agency said.

title: The Biggest Names in Fine Dining Now Have Rock-Star Residencies
partialText: From Las Vegas to the Côte d’Azur, high-profile chefs are taking their cuisine on the road.

title: In an Asymmetrical War, Iran Seeks an Edge With Its Information War
partialText: Propaganda and disinformation have flooded the internet in a sophisticated effort to undermine support for U.S. and Israeli attacks.

title: The Oil Shocks of the ’70s Changed the World. Will the Iran War Do the Same?
partialText: Gas lines and quadrupling oil prices freaked out American consumers. But the oil crises also transformed global finance.

title: Smaller Is Better in Silicon Valley’s ‘Tiny Team’ Moment
partialText: As artificial intelligence takes on more and more tasks, tech executives are embracing teams as small as two: one person plus A.I.

title: Can This Russian Bakery Survive a 3,500% Tax Increase?
partialText: The challenges faced by a small-business owner near Moscow highlight how Russia’s war-drained economy is on the doorstep of a major crisis.

title: Bank of America to Pay $72.5 Million to Settle Lawsuit by Epstein Victims
partialText: The suit claimed the bank had overlooked signs that Mr. Epstein’s accounts were being used to further his abuse of young women.

title: Trump Offers More Aid to Farmers, a Key Support Bloc Hurt by Tariffs and War
partialText: The president announced new loan guarantees at a White House event that appeared intended to reassure a group that has found itself caught in the crosshairs of some of his major policies.

title: Elon Musk Joins in Phone Call Between Donald Trump and Narendra Modi
partialText: Mr. Musk’s participation was notable because it is rare for a private citizen to be on a call between heads of state. It also suggests that Mr. Musk is back on better terms with the president.

title: Iran Moves to Formalize Toll Plan in Strait of Hormuz
partialText: Tehran has effectively closed off the critical waterway, turning back container ships on Friday, and Iranian lawmakers are considering whether to formalize charging fees to pass.

title: Stocks Keep Falling as Investor Lose Patience With the War in Iran
partialText: The S&P 500 is down nearly 9 percent from a January high. The weekly losing streak is its worst in roughly four years.

title: Versant, Owner of MS NOW, in Talks to Acquire Vox Media’s Podcast Division
partialText: Versant, the parent company of CNBC and MS NOW, is looking to continue expanding its business beyond cable TV.

title: Global Food Supply Faces a Dangerous Bottleneck as Iran War Persists
partialText: Fertilizer prices are climbing as a result of disruptions in the Middle East, putting global food supplies at risk.

title: The Iran War Has Diesel Prices Soaring, and Consumers Could Pay the Price
partialText: Diesel has climbed faster than gasoline this month, directly hitting businesses, from brewers to trucking companies. Those higher costs are likely to make their way into consumer prices.

title: Many People Will Need Long-Term Care, but Most Don’t Have Insurance to Cover It
partialText: Care for people who can’t take care of themselves is expensive, and regular health insurance doesn’t cover the cost.
